description:
The Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme was launched in India on October 2, 1975. 

The primary aim of the ICDS scheme is to provide food, preschool education, and primary healthcare to children under the age of six years. 

The program also targets pregnant women and lactating mothers. 

In Uttarakhand, the ICDS scheme was implemented with the objective of improving the nutritional and health status of children. 

The scheme aims to reduce mortality, morbidity, and malnutrition among children. 

It also seeks to enhance the growth and development of children through a comprehensive approach. 

The ICDS program in Uttarakhand is managed by the Department of Women Empowerment and Child Development. 

The scheme operates through a network of Anganwadi centers across the state. 

As of October 2023, there are approximately 15,000 Anganwadi centers in Uttarakhand. 

These centers serve around 1.5 million children and 500,000 pregnant and lactating women. 

The benefits of the ICDS scheme include supplementary nutrition, health check-ups, immunization, and preschool education. 

Under the supplementary nutrition program, children receive a daily meal that includes a specific quantity of protein and calories. 

Children aged 6 months to 3 years receive 500 calories and 12-15 grams of protein per day. 

Children aged 3 to 6 years receive 600 calories and 12-15 grams of protein per day. 

Pregnant women and lactating mothers receive 600 calories and 18-20 grams of protein per day. 

The nutritional supplements are provided in the form of take-home rations or hot cooked meals. 

The scheme also includes health check-ups for children and mothers. 

Regular health check-ups are conducted at Anganwadi centers to monitor growth and development. 

Immunization services are provided to ensure that children receive all necessary vaccinations. 

The ICDS scheme also focuses on early childhood education. 

Children aged 3 to 6 years are provided with preschool education to prepare them for formal schooling. 

The educational component includes activities that promote cognitive and social development. 

Eligibility for the ICDS scheme includes children aged 0 to 6 years, pregnant women, and lactating mothers. 

There are no specific income criteria for eligibility. 

All families with children in the target age group can access the services. 

The application process for the ICDS scheme is straightforward. 

Parents or guardians can approach the nearest Anganwadi center to enroll their children. 

Required documents typically include proof of age for the child and identity proof for the parent or guardian. 

The ICDS scheme operates year-round with no specific application deadlines. 

Services are provided continuously to eligible beneficiaries. 

The implementing authority for the ICDS scheme in Uttarakhand is the Department of Women Empowerment and Child Development. 

The department can be contacted through its official website for more information. 

The ICDS scheme in Uttarakhand has seen significant improvements in child health indicators. 

According to the National Family Health Survey 5 conducted in 2019-2020, the stunting rate among children under five in Uttarakhand was 30.4 percent. 

The wasting rate was reported at 15.4 percent. 

The scheme has contributed to increasing the immunization coverage among children. 

As of 2023, immunization coverage in Uttarakhand stands at approximately 90 percent for basic vaccines. 

The ICDS scheme is also aligned with the National Nutrition Mission launched in 2018. 

The mission aims to reduce stunting, undernutrition, and anemia among children and women. 

The ICDS scheme plays a crucial role in achieving these national targets. 

The program is funded by both the central and state governments. 

The funding is allocated based on the number of beneficiaries and operational costs of Anganwadi centers. 

The central government contributes a significant portion of the funding. 

In Uttarakhand, the state government has also increased its budget allocation for the ICDS scheme in recent years. 

For the financial year 2023-2024, the budget allocation for the scheme was approximately INR 500 crores. 

This funding is utilized for various activities including nutrition provision, training of Anganwadi workers, and infrastructure development. 

The ICDS scheme also emphasizes community participation. 

Local self-governments and community organizations are encouraged to participate in the implementation of the scheme. 

This involvement helps in tailoring services to meet local needs. 

The scheme has been instrumental in raising awareness about nutrition and health among communities. 

Workshops and training sessions are conducted for parents and caregivers. 

These sessions focus on the importance of nutrition, hygiene, and early childhood development. 

The ICDS scheme in Uttarakhand has also faced challenges. 

Issues such as inadequate infrastructure and shortage of trained staff have been reported. 

Efforts are being made to address these challenges through capacity building and resource allocation. 

Regular monitoring and evaluation are conducted to assess the impact of the scheme. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve service delivery. 

The ICDS scheme is a vital component of the social welfare framework in Uttarakhand. 

It plays a significant role in ensuring the health and development of children and mothers. 

The scheme's comprehensive approach addresses multiple aspects of child welfare. 

This includes nutrition, health, and education. 

The ICDS scheme continues to evolve to meet the changing needs of the population. 

It remains committed to achieving its objectives of improving child health and nutrition in Uttarakhand. 

The ongoing efforts of the government and local communities are crucial for the success of the scheme. 

The ICDS scheme is a testament to India's commitment to child welfare and development. 

It reflects the government's dedication to building a healthier and more educated future generation. 

Through the ICDS scheme, the government aims to create a supportive environment for children and mothers. 

This initiative is essential for fostering the overall development of society.
